scope_incompatibilities.difference: AEO isolates server electricity; IEA/LBNL include servers, storage, networking, and infrastructure such as cooling and power conversion.
scope_incompatibilities.allowed_comparison: side-by-side with an explicit scope badge
scope_incompatibilities.disallowed_comparison: single uninterrupted line or direct growth calculation across the two measures

scope_incompatibilities.difference: Different models, geography, sector boundaries, and final-energy accounting.
scope_incompatibilities.allowed_comparison: separate U.S. and world views with definitions

scope_incompatibilities.difference: Ember defines demand as gross generation plus net imports; IEA's Electricity 2026 milestone is final consumption.
scope_incompatibilities.allowed_comparison: parallel historical-system-demand and final-consumption views with scope labels
scope_incompatibilities.disallowed_comparison: joining the two values into one continuous historical/forecast line or presenting the difference as an error

scope_incompatibilities.difference: Energy volume does not identify hourly coincidence or capacity requirement.
scope_incompatibilities.disallowed_comparison: inferring peak or reliability directly from annual TWh

scope_incompatibilities.difference: Model baseline/conditional values are not observations and may differ in definition or vintage.
scope_incompatibilities.allowed_comparison: visible historical/scenario seam at 2025 with separate source styling
scope_incompatibilities.disallowed_comparison: continuous observed-looking line without a seam

hierarchy_rules.rule: Stack exactly one hierarchy level: total sectors, buildings subsectors, transportation subsectors, or industry subsectors. Do not stack sector totals with their children.
For industrial purchased electricity, use total or the three disjoint components (excluding refining/hydrogen, refining, hydrogen production), never both.
Residential and commercial gross end-use subtotals, purchased electricity, on-site generation, and named end uses are accounting layers, not a single additive stack.
